## Fix list (highest priority first)

1. **CLU-04 — Kubernetes version current**: cluster version 1.31 is past standard support (floor is 1.32) — plan an upgrade; EKS auto-upgrades extended-support clusters and bills for it
1. **CLU-06 — Public API endpoint restricted**: public endpoint allows 0.0.0.0/0 (variable default) — anyone on the internet can reach the API server; restrict cluster_endpoint_public_access_cidrs to your IPs
1. **CLU-07 — PodDisruptionBudget present**: no PodDisruptionBudget in kubernetes/ or apps/ — node drains and upgrades can take all replicas down at once
1. **ARG-07 — ArgoCD high availability**: ArgoCD components run with 1 replica — a node failure takes the GitOps controller down (deploys pause until it returns)
1. **IAM-03 — No over-broad IAM policies**: wildcard actions or resources appear in a policy — check the tfsec ignore comment justifies them (read-only Describe/List actions legitimately need resource *)
1. **VPC-03 — NAT gateway per AZ**: single_nat_gateway is true — one NAT gateway serves all AZs; if its AZ fails, outbound traffic stops. Acceptable for dev, not for prod
1. **MON-04 — Alertmanager routes alerts somewhere**: Alertmanager is enabled but no receiver (Slack, email, PagerDuty, webhook) is configured — alerts fire and go nowhere
1. **OPS-01 — Terraform remote state**: no S3 backend in terraform/ — state lives locally; a lost laptop means a lost state file
1. **OPS-02 — Ingress controller present**: Ingress uses class nginx but no ingress controller is declared in the repo — the Ingress will stay unimplemented until one is installed

See `docs/checks.md` in the eks-gitops-doctor repo for what each check
looks at, why it matters, and how to fix it.
